examDayRules.title: Registration and booking
examDayRules.detail: Register at certifications.nism.ac.in with scanned PAN and recent colour passport photo (not older than 6 months), activate via email link. Then New Enrollment > choose exam, city, test centre, date/slot > pay online (card/net banking). Enrolment closes 48 hours before the exam; enrolment is valid for 180 days. Soft-copy workbook free within 24 hours of enrolment; printed workbook via Taxmann (~Rs 250 + courier).

examDayRules.title: ID proof
examDayRules.detail: Admit card (physical or soft copy) + one ORIGINAL photo ID: PAN, Aadhaar, driving licence or passport. DigiLocker copies with embedded photo accepted. Registration guidelines also mention carrying a self-attested PAN copy. Name/photo mismatch = entry refused with no refund.

examDayRules.title: Reporting time
examDayRules.detail: Reach the test centre 30 minutes before the slot. Late arrivals may be refused and marked absent with no refund or reschedule.

examDayRules.title: Calculator and Excel
examDayRules.detail: At test centres you may bring your own silent calculator with no connectivity (all types allowed). Workstations provide MS Excel or LibreOffice for calculations (stated for V-D and NISM's AIF-manager prep guide). Remote-proctored exams provide an on-screen scientific calculator; no physical calculator allowed.

examDayRules.title: Rough sheets
examDayRules.detail: Use only rough sheets issued by the invigilator; return them before leaving. No rough sheets in remote-proctored exams.

examDayRules.title: Prohibited items
examDayRules.detail: Phones, tablets, smartwatches, Bluetooth devices, books/notes, food (water allowed). Keep devices switched off in locker.

examDayRules.title: Rescheduling
examDayRules.detail: Self-reschedule via portal at least 4 days before the exam (registration guide also says 15 days and only once - the published refund policy says 4 days and a cap of two reschedules). Change of module is NOT allowed. No-show = fee forfeited.

examDayRules.title: Refunds
examDayRules.detail: Fees are non-refundable except for failed/duplicate payment or test administrator unable to conduct exam. Payment gateway/transaction charges never refunded.

examDayRules.title: Results and scorecard
examDayRules.detail: Result shown on screen at end; collect scorecard from invigilator before leaving (issued once). No re-evaluation; you may challenge up to two specific questions on the spot before leaving the centre.

examDayRules.title: Certificate
examDayRules.detail: Soft copy only, issued in 10-15 working days, downloadable from the portal/emailed; requires PAN verified against Income Tax database. Valid 3 years from exam pass date.

examDayRules.title: Retakes
examDayRules.detail: No waiting period between failed attempts is specified by NISM - re-enrol and pay again. A candidate who has passed may re-sit only for renewal, within the last 12 months of validity.

examDayRules.title: Remote proctoring status
examDayRules.detail: NISM discontinued remote-proctored certification exams from Jan 1, 2023 (test centres only). NISM published updated remote-proctored exam instructions/FAQs in Jul 2026 (Mettl), and renewal exams X-C/XV-B and eCPEs are online-proctored. Which full exams are currently bookable remotely is not stated - check the portal at booking.

examDayRules.title: Remote-proctored technical requirements
examDayRules.detail: Windows 7+ laptop/desktop only (no Mac/Linux/mobile), internal webcam + mic, 512 kbps+ stable internet, Mercer Mettl Secure Browser (MSB), pop-ups allowed, antivirus/firewall disabled, single screen, phone placed ~1 m to the side as second camera, quiet lit room. Start Test link active from 15 min before to 15 min after slot. No breaks. Renewal exams (X-C/XV-B) need Windows 10+, 4 GB RAM, i3 5th gen+, 2 Mbps.

examDayRules.title: Helpdesk
examDayRules.detail: NISM: certification@nism.ac.in, +91 8080806476. Remote proctoring (Mettl): 080-47190902, mettl-support@mercer.com. Printed workbooks: Taxmann sales.mumbai@taxmann.com.

prepStrategy.title: Workbook first, latest version
prepStrategy.detail: NISM questions are drawn from the official workbook. Download the current version (check the version/date on page 1) - XV (Jan 2026), XXI-A (Mar 2025) and V-D (Mar 2026 material) were all revised recently. NISM's own advice: do not enrol until you have read the workbook thoroughly, two or three passes for long workbooks (XIX-C is 550+ pages).

prepStrategy.title: Book the date to create a deadline
prepStrategy.detail: Enrolment is valid 180 days; book a slot ~3-6 weeks out (2h papers) or 6-8 weeks out (3h papers) and work backwards. Reschedules need 4+ days notice.

prepStrategy.title: Weight chapters by the test objectives
prepStrategy.detail: Each exam's test-objectives annexure gives marks per chapter (e.g. V-D: MF 68, Equity Derivatives 52, IRD 30). Spend time in proportion to marks and depth of numericals; high-weight regulatory and product chapters first.

prepStrategy.title: Master numericals and Excel
prepStrategy.detail: Rework every illustrative example (returns, XIRR, bond pricing/duration, option payoffs, futures pricing, tax, retirement corpus). Practise Excel functions (FV, PV, PMT, RATE, NPV, XIRR, STDEV) because Excel/LibreOffice is on the exam workstation.

prepStrategy.title: Caselet technique
prepStrategy.detail: Read the questions first, then the case, so you know what data to extract. Note key numbers on the rough sheet. Caselet questions in X-A/X-B/XIX-C/XXI-B carry 2 marks - and 2x the penalty - so do them in a calm pass after banking the 1-mark MCQs.

prepStrategy.title: Two-pass time management
prepStrategy.detail: 3h paper with ~120-150 items: ~1.2-1.4 min per item. Pass 1 (about 60% of time): answer all sure items, flag doubtful ones. Pass 2: caselets and flagged numericals. Last 10 min: review flags only, do not change answers without a clear reason. 2h/100 items: ~1 min per item; same pattern.

prepStrategy.title: Mock tests as diagnostics
prepStrategy.detail: Take NISM portal mock tests plus 3-5 full timed mocks. Target 75%+ in mocks before the real attempt to cover the 60% pass mark plus negative-marking leakage. Log every wrong answer by chapter and revisit the workbook text, not just the answer key.

prepStrategy.title: Spaced repetition and revision cadence
prepStrategy.detail: Make flashcards for numbers that are pure recall (limits, timelines, thresholds, regulation names, fee caps). Review on day 1, 3, 7, 14. Do a full skim of chapter summaries in the final 48 hours; the final evening is for formulas and regulatory numbers only.

prepStrategy.title: Leverage overlaps
prepStrategy.detail: Sequence exams so later papers reuse earlier study (see overlaps). Sitting related exams 2-4 weeks apart keeps shared content warm.

whyPeopleFail: Studying from summary notes or question dumps instead of the current workbook - questions test exact workbook wording, limits and timelines.
Using an outdated workbook after a revision (XV Jan 2026, XXI-A Mar 2025, V-D Jul 2026).
Wild guessing under 25% negative marking, especially on 2-mark caselet questions where a wrong answer costs 0.5.
Running out of time on caselets in 3-hour papers by doing them first or re-reading cases.
Weak numericals and Excel handling (XIRR, bond maths, option payoffs, financial planning calculations).
Skipping low-interest regulatory chapters that carry many easy marks.
Not taking full timed mocks, so the 60% pass threshold is not tested under exam conditions.
Underestimating 'foundation-looking' papers and booking too early.
negativeMarkingPolicy: NISM questions are typically 4-option MCQs. Let p = probability your chosen answer is correct, mark value m, penalty fraction f. EV of answering = p*m - (1-p)*f*m; answer when p > f/(1+f). (1) 25% negative (X-A, X-B, VIII, XV, XVII, XIX-C/D/E, XXI-A, XXI-B): break-even p = 0.20. Blind guess (p=0.25) EV = 0.25 - 0.75*0.25 = +0.0625 per mark; eliminate 1 option (p=0.33) EV = +0.167; eliminate 2 (p=0.5) EV = +0.375. So guessing is mildly positive even blind, but high-variance; guess whenever you can eliminate at least one option, and skip only true blind guesses if you are already comfortably above 60%. The ratio is identical for 2-mark caselet questions (gain 2, lose 0.5). NISM's own AIF prep note warns against 'wild guessing'. (2) 10% negative (V-D, XIX-A, XIX-B): break-even p = 0.091; blind guess EV = 0.25 - 0.75*0.10 = +0.175 - always answer every question. (3) 0% negative (V-B, X-C, XV-B renewal): never leave a question blank.

overlaps.detail: SEBI requires both; X-A covers financial planning foundations, products, tax, retirement and regulation; X-B goes deeper on asset allocation, portfolio construction, valuation, behavioural finance and case-based advice. Take X-A first, X-B within weeks. X-C is the renewal route once both are held.

V-D = V-A (MF) content ~45% + Equity Derivatives (Series VIII) ~35% + Interest Rate Derivatives (Series IV) ~20%. Doing VIII first covers about a third of V-D. Savin already has V-A, so V-D is essentially V-A refresh + VIII + IRD.
V-B is a subset-level foundation of MF content already covered by V-A/V-D; low value for someone who has passed V-A.

All share the SEBI AIF Regulations 2012, AIF categories, fund structures, fee/waterfall, taxation and distribution norms. XIX-A (Cat I/II) and XIX-B (Cat III) are 2h distributor papers; XIX-C is the 3h manager paper covering both plus portfolio theory, valuation and performance metrics. Sequence A -> B -> C (or D/E as category-specific manager alternatives).

Both built on SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, PMS structure, fees, reporting and investment approaches; XXI-B adds portfolio management theory, valuation and fund-management decision-making. Do XXI-A then XXI-B.

Shared quantitative core: equity valuation (DCF, multiples), fixed income maths, risk-return, portfolio theory and performance measurement. XV (RA) adds financial statement analysis and research report norms.
Retirement planning (corpus, annuities, NPS, PFRDA products) appears in X-A's financial planning content; XVII is a deeper retirement/PFRDA-specific paper.
Largely standalone (exchange-traded equity derivatives, trading/clearing/settlement, risk management) except its overlap with V-D's derivatives modules.
